what_happened: The job asked to make planning a real per-item pass that flags underspecified requests. It was rejected. The verifier failed 7 of 10 acceptance criteria. Six of the unmet criteria were cargo test behaviors: flagging a vague request, not copying the first line into acceptance, inferring or refusing a rung, filling open_questions, grouping items that touch the same path, and a drain test that refuses a vague item. The seventh was a user-invokable `athena plan` command exercised with `cargo run`. There were two blocker or major findings. The major finding was that the evidence for behavior criterion 7 did not cite commands that ran (D43). The blocker was that the disk in the verifier environment was full, so no behavior criterion could be exercised. The event lists no failed checks. The planning work itself was not shown to be wrong. The verifier could not run anything, so the criteria were left unproven.
cause: Nothing checks that the verifier's environment can build and run tests before verification starts, and nothing separates an environment failure from a work failure. Cargo builds fill disk, and artifacts from earlier jobs and verifier snapshots build up with no cleanup or free-space limit. A full disk was therefore found only when the verifier tried to run, and the verdict was recorded as a failure of the job, with every criterion unmet. The system has no verdict for "could not verify", so the only outcome available was rejection. This is an inference from the blocker finding, since the stored fields do not show disk usage or what filled it.
prevention: Add a preflight code check before verification. It would require a minimum amount of free disk space in the verifier workspace and a trivial build or test command that succeeds. If the check fails, Athena would clean up build artifacts (such as old target directories and snapshots) and retry. If that fails too, the job would be marked as an "unverified, environment" state and re-queued, not rejected. A job would count as rejected only when the verifier actually ran. A disk-space check would also run again after the build. This would have prevented the whole class, because a broken environment would never be recorded as a failed job.
proposed_request: Make Athena's verification robust to an unusable verifier environment. Before the verifier starts, check that the verifier workspace has enough free disk space and that a trivial cargo build and test succeeds. If space is low, clean build artifacts and old verifier snapshots that are no longer needed, then check again. If the environment is still unusable, do not record the job as rejected. Mark it as unverified because of the environment, tell the operator the reason, and let it be re-verified once the environment is fixed, without redoing the build. Add cargo tests that show (1) a low-space preflight triggers cleanup and then passes, (2) a persistent failure gives the unverified-environment state, not a rejection, and a re-verify run can start from it, and (3) a normal job is verified as before. Then re-run job 20261016-hem1's request, "Make planning a real per-item pass that flags underspecified requests", so that its 10 acceptance criteria, including the `athena plan` command exercised with `cargo run`, are verified with evidence citing the commands that ran.
